question: True or false: a clinic fridge that read 2 to 8 °C at every twice-daily check has probably not frozen its vaccines?
answer: False. Two readings a day sample two moments; a dip below zero between them leaves no trace. In a Connecticut study, freeze indicators on vaccine boxes tripped in 40 of 45 clinic fridges over 24 weeks. Logs showed 2 to 8 °C before all but one event, and a thermometer caught just one freeze.
move: A check made at fixed times sees nothing that happens between them.
trap: Treating a clean logbook as proof the fridge stayed in range.
source: Infectious Diseases in Clinical Practice, freeze study
